'''Ochotl''' was an [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Agriworld/Legends|agriworld]] located in the [[Airam sector/Legends|Airam sector]]. The company [[Ochotl Ag]] [[Farm/Legends|harvested]] the [[Chak-root/Legends|chak-root]] [[Plant/Legends|plant]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]], which was also the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]-renowned [[Shockball/Legends|shockball]] player [[Kob Mondray]].

At some point by [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], Ochotl Ag's competitors set into motion events that devastated the future prospects of the company, which was further compounded by a [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] attack that destroyed Ochotl's [[Space station/Legends|orbital depots]]. Following the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|outbreak]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Ochotl and the rest of the Airam [[Sector/Legends|sector]] left the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and joined the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]].

==Description==
Ochotl was an [[Agriworld/Legends|agricultural planet]]<ref name="Author's Cut" /> located in the [[Ochotl system/Legends|Ochotl system]], a part of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Airam sector/Legends|Airam sector]].<ref name="EAOC Ochotl" /> It was situated outside the location known as [[The Pangarees/Legends|the Pangarees]] and was [[Orbit/Legends|circled]] by [[Space station/Legends|orbital depots]]. On Ochotl, the company [[Ochotl Ag]] [[Farm/Legends|harvested]] [[Chak-root/Legends|chak-root]],<ref name="Author's Cut" /> a [[Plant/Legends|plant]] originating from<ref name="Guide">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Third Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> [[Erysthes]].<ref name="Guide" />

==History==
Ochotl was the [[Homeworld/Legends|birth world]] of the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Kob Mondray]], who eventually became a [[Shockball/Legends|shockball]] player. In [[31 BBY/Legends|31 BBY]], he led [[Ochotl Ag's corporate team|Ochotl Ag's corporate shockball team]] to participate in the [[Airam Sector Championships]]. That marked the start of Mondray's shockball career that over the subsequent [[Standard year/Legends|years]] led him to become a [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] celebrity&mdash;although, despite his amassed wealth and luxurious residences on such worlds as [[Kuat/Legends|Kuat]] and [[Spira/Legends|Spira]], the [[Athlete/Legends|athlete]] never felt comfortable in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

[[File:Chakrootpic.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The Ochotl-based company Ochotl Ag exported chak-root (pictured) harvests off-world.]]
In order to better compete with the agricultural companies of the Pangarees, at some point by [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], Ochotl Ag became a member of the [[Corporate Alliance/Legends|Corporate Alliance]]. The competitors of the Ochotl-based firm, however, had influence with the [[Supreme Court/Legends|courts]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], and an investigation was launched into a possible infestation of Ochotl by<ref name="Author's Cut" /> the creatures<ref name="TCW">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' novelization]]</ref> known as [[Corris weevil|Corris-weevils]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

Although no evidence for the infestation was discovered, Ochotl was placed on a three-year probationary list, and Ochotl Ag lost its entire chak-root crop, with the market for its goods effectively having been destroyed. Furthermore, while the Corporate Alliance was attempting to have Ochotl's case [[Judge/Legends|arbitrated]], [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] based at [[Nocto]],<ref name="Author's Cut" /> in the [[Nocto system/Legends|Nocto system]],<ref name="TEA" /> destroyed the depots in orbit around Ochotl. The [[Outland Regions Security Force/Legends|Republic Outland Regions Security Force]], which was also indirectly linked to Ochotl Ag's competitors, only made half-hearted attempts to respond to the attack.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

In 22 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]], the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] between the Republic and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], of which the Corporate Alliance was a member, [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|broke out]].<ref name="TEA" /> Subsequently,<ref name="Sports" /> the entire Airam [[Sector/Legends|sector]],<ref name="Author's Cut" /> including Ochotl, seceded from the Republic and joined the Confederacy,<ref name="Sports" /> and in 22 BBY,<ref name="22 BBY">{{SW|url=news/take-me-out-to-the-ballgame-sports-in-the-star-wars-galaxy-part-2|series=Sports in the Star Wars Galaxy|text=Part 2: Take Me Out to the Ball Game|nolive=1}} establishes that [[Kob Mondray]] entered [[Confederacy military/Legends|military service]] on the side of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] following the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|beginning]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], which ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' dates to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]. In addition, {{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 8: Tales of the Clone Wars}} states that Mondray was already fighting as part of the Confederacy during that same [[Standard year/Legends|year]], thereby firmly placing his joining the Confederacy in 22 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]].</ref> Mondray, who had become troubled by his homeworld's plight while it was still part of the Republic, also announced the end of his career in shockball in favor of serving as part of the [[Confederacy military/Legends|Confederacy military]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

==Behind the scenes==
Ochotl was originally meant to be mentioned in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]]; however, the section that would have mentioned the planet was cut before the book's release.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

The information regarding Ochotl was later released in [[2014]] as part of [[Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut]], a series of articles published on the [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars Blog|Blog]] by Fry and<ref name="Author's Cut" /> [[Del Rey]] editor<ref name="Celestials">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut — The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref> [[Erich Schoeneweiss]] containing various cut content from ''The Essential Guide to Warfare''.<ref name="Author's Cut" /> The StarWars.com [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|Online Companion]] to the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Ochotl [[Star system/Legends|system]], and therefore the planet itself, in grid square L-20.<ref name="EAOC Ochotl" />
